title: Tenaris unveils well string donated to Norsk Oljemuseum

The donated well string installation represents longstanding relations between Tenaris and Norway's energy community.


Tenaris


Tenaris has donated a complete well string to Norsk Oljemuseum in Stavanger, Norway, strengthening its long-standing connection with the local energy community and contributing to the museum’s educational mission.


The installation was officially unveiled in November during an event that brought together Tenaris customers, museum officials, local stakeholders, and company representatives to celebrate more than 40 years of Tenaris’s presence in Norway and its relationship with the Norwegian energy industry.


The well string illustrates the typical structure of an oil and gas well, from surface casing to production tubing, and features Tenaris proprietary premium connections TenarisHydril Blue® and Wedge 623® with Dopeless® technology, Tenaris’s leading dope-free solution for running operations. Developed in collaboration with Norwegian operators, the technology was first introduced in 2005.


"We are grateful to Tenaris for this second collaboration, which builds on the well string exhibit donated to the museum in 2012," said **Leif Harald Halvorsen** , Exhibition Manager at Norsk Oljemuseum. "The new well string offers a complete and raw view of how casing and connections are assembled from top to bottom, and it will serve as an important educational resource for students, families, and the wider public."


Each year, approximately 160,000 people visit Norsk Oljemuseum to learn about Norway’s petroleum heritage. As part of the museum’s permanent exhibition, the well string will offer visitors and future generations a tangible way to understand the engineering and technologies behind offshore well construction.


"Tenaris came to Norway more than 40 years ago, and we have grown together with the industry and the people of Stavanger," said **Christer Andersen** , Tenaris Commercial Director North Sea. "Being part of a community for that long means contributing to its progress through education, culture, and opportunities for future generations. Helping the museum preserve this piece of our shared industrial history is a natural part of that commitment."


The donation continues a relationship that began more than a decade ago and reflects the company's support for culture and learning wherever it operates.
